hook: Swift continuations hide the nastiest concurrency bugs.

beats.say: Most iOS codebases still have callback APIs at their edges: an analytics SDK, a Bluetooth stack, a payment library, or an old networking layer nobody wants to rewrite.
Continuations are how those APIs become async functions. The conversion looks trivial, but it is where the author has seen the most subtle concurrency bugs.
The bugs are tasks that hang forever and sudden crashes, including the double resume problem, which the article fixes by taking the continuation under a lock.
